page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at the top, right of centre, with the page number at the top right. Below the text, at the foot: a gathering signature at left-centre and a Greek catchword at the right.

main_text.p: 2. Συναίτιον[?] precum fidei recte dixerimus esse, mandatum Dei de inuocatione & eius forma. Vt enim Lex caussa impulsiua est, quia (ut optimus ille Melanchthō dicere solebat) est cogitatio agentis, qua impellitur ad agendum: ita mandatū, Dominum Deum tuum adorabis: impel-lit inuocantem ad ferias preces, ac simul docet quis inuocandus sit, & quomodo.
3. Σύνπιστις[?] fides excitata à Spiritu sancto, & in mandatum pariter & promissionem de exauditione respiciens. Ideo ἐὐχὴ[?] τῆς πίστεως[?] dicitur, Iac.5.15.

4. Forma eius scite descripsit idem Apostolus, Epistolae suae cap.1.v.6, Αἰτείτω ἐν πίστει, μηδὲν διακρινόμενος, ὁ γὰρ διακρινόμενος ἔοικε κλύδωνι θαλάσσης ἀνεμιζομένῳ καὶ ῥιπιζομένῳ. Sed postulet cum fide nihil disceptas; nam qui disceptat, similis est fluctui maris, qui ventis agitatur & iactatur.

5. Proximi fines precum, monstrantes diversas species, peti possunt ex illo nobili dicto Pauli, 1.Tim.2.1. Adhortor igitur ante omnia, ut fiant deprecationes, preces, postulationes, gratiarum actiones pro quibusuis hominibus.

page.notes: Long s is printed as s throughout. The Greek words in paragraphs 2 and 3 are only partly legible and are marked [?]; the Greek of paragraph 4 is from Jas 1:6 as printed and is copied with its accents but the first word is uncertain. The word "caussa" is printed with a double-s ligature. The gathering signature and the Greek catchword at the foot are faint. "impel-lit" has a printed hyphen at the line end; "impulsiua" has none and is written whole.
